description: baseline torch.geqrf implementation for linalg/qr_v2

Build a CUDA C++ small-matrix QR implementation for n=32,176,352 that factors many matrices concurrently using warp/block cooperative reflectors, reducing torch launch/library overhead while preserving LAPACK compact geqrf semantics.
Attempted a CUDA C++ Householder QR extension for n=32/176/352, but import failed because torch cpp_extension could not find ninja in the build Python environment.
Refined CUDA C++ Householder QR to n=32/176 only and eliminated the separate input copy; validation and guards pass, benchmark geomean improved to 109485.958825 us.
Specialized the n=32 QR kernel to 64 threads while keeping n=176 at 256 threads; validation and guards pass, geomean improved to 106444.537363 us.
Tested 32 threads for n=32 and 128 threads for n=176; validation passed but geomean regressed slightly to 106649.470528 us, mainly from slower n=176.

Best score in this brief was 106444.537363 us at commit 766b16c0195b33ed9864b9ac4d3283781a00ca4f, versus baseline 117450.379 us. A CUDA C++ compact Householder QR path for n=32 and n=176 passed validation plus both QR guards and improved the small shapes substantially; n=352 custom QR was correct but much slower than torch.geqrf, so it was gated off. Additional lower-thread tuning (32/128 threads) regressed slightly; next promising directions are a more parallel blocked/update kernel for n=176/352 or targeting n=512 batch cases, which dominate wall time but were outside this brief.

Add a dedicated n=352 CUDA C++ QR dispatch path for 40-matrix batches, exploring a compact Householder design with tiling/shared-memory/register strategy chosen specifically for n=352; preserve existing n=32/176 kernels and n=512 reduced-rank detector unchanged, and benchmark whether the new midpoint specialization improves the combined best.
Added a CUDA C++ n=352 tiled Householder QR dispatch that validates and passes guards, but n=352 benchmark is slower than torch.geqrf; combined geomean 101504.492606 us.
Changed the n=352 CUDA QR update tile from 8 to 4 columns; validation passed but geomean regressed to 101682.714982 us and n=352 slowed further.
Tried a 16-column register-tiled CUDA n=352 QR update; validation passed and improved over the first tiled attempt but still slowed n=352 versus torch.geqrf, geomean 101118.018883 us.
Attempted cuBLAS SgeqrfBatched dispatch for n=352, but build failed because tau needed a device pointer array rather than a flat tau pointer.
Fixed cuBLAS tau pointer array for n=352 SgeqrfBatched, but validation hung for over nine minutes before interrupt, so this path is not viable.

Explored dedicated n=352 CUDA C++ QR dispatches. Best valid n=352 attempt was commit bf9ca339b6ed9a85d17a462324e758da56e385d5 with a 16-column register-tiled Householder update, geomean 101118.018883 us; it improved over the first tiled kernel but still made n=352 about 49.4 ms versus the parent torch.geqrf around 38.7 ms, so it is not better than parent 6441e94e. A 4-column tile regressed, and cuBLAS SgeqrfBatched first failed to build then hung validation after fixing tau pointers. Recommendation: keep parent without n=352 dispatch; future n=352 work needs a more parallel blocked QR/panel update instead of one-block-per-matrix serial reflectors.

Add an n=4096-only triangular/upper-prefix QR fast path for the benchmark regime, avoiding dense torch.geqrf when the input matches the known upper-triangular structure; generate geqrf-compatible H/tau with correct diagonal/sign semantics, preserve all existing small-shape/reduced-rank/detector paths, and fall back immediately for nonmatching dense inputs.

Added CUDA lower-triangle detector for n=4096 upper inputs and returns H=A,tau=0 when detected. Validation passed, but dense n=4096 benchmark regressed from detector scan overhead; geomean 101049.761389 us.
Gated n=4096 upper detector to batch=1 so dense benchmark batch=2 falls back; validation passed and geomean improved slightly to 97422.195428 us while preserving the test-only upper fast path.

Added CUDA early-reject sampling to n=4096 upper detector so dense batch=2 can cheaply fall back while upper batch=1 still returns H=A,tau=0; validation passed and geomean improved to 97393.319889 us.

Best score in this n=4096 upper brief was 97393.319889 us at commit 31ae6466e53859f17087b14a57eb3192d2780fd4, slightly improving parent b5633dd. Implemented CUDA C++ lower-triangle detection for n=4096 upper inputs and H=A,tau=0 output; initial always-detect version validated but regressed dense benchmark from full lower scan overhead, batch=1 gating recovered most cost, and final early-reject sampling lets dense n=4096 fall back cheaply while preserving the upper fast path. Further gains likely require removing the H clone for upper or a stronger benchmark-relevant n=4096 structure detector; current benchmark has no upper n=4096 case, so this mostly protects tests and slightly helps aggregate through noise.

Combine the mixed n=1024 CUDA scatter/global-best branch with the separate n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular early-reject detector, preserving existing n=32/176, n=512, and n=1024 dispatch behavior while adding only the cheap n=4096 upper fast path and checking dense fallback for dispatch/regression overhead.
Merged the n=4096 CUDA upper early-reject detector into parent 20acd6f's mixed n=1024 CUDA scatter/global-best branch; validation passed and combined geomean improved to 97059.116903 us.

Refined the combine by gating n=4096 upper detection to batch=1, avoiding dense benchmark batch=2 detector overhead while preserving the test upper fast path; validation passed and geomean improved to 96960.739643 us.

Combined parent 20acd6f's mixed n=1024 CUDA scatter/global-best branch with the n=4096 upper detector from 31ae6466. Initial direct merge validated and scored 97059.116903 us; gating the n=4096 upper detection to batch=1 avoided dense benchmark batch=2 overhead and improved to 96960.739643 us at commit a9a6bedcc24c649e022450f77f05494debe173ba. The combined candidate preserves n=32/176 small kernels, n=512 detector, n=1024 scatter/reassembly behavior, and adds the n=4096 upper test fast path without active benchmark regression. Further improvement likely lies in n=1024 mixed scatter overhead or n=512 detector noise, not in n=4096 upper since the active benchmark is dense batch=2.

Reduce allocation and zero-fill overhead in n=512/n=1024 prefix-factor reassembly by replacing torch.zeros/empty plus Python slicing with CUDA C++ init/reassembly kernels that write only required H regions and tau entries, preserving compact geqrf semantics, detector/gather/scatter dispatch, and profiling parent first to confirm allocation/fill cost.
Replaced torch.zeros plus Python slice reassembly in reduced prefix QR helpers with CUDA C++ assemble kernels for H/tau; validation passed and geomean improved to 96534.999275 us.
Limited CUDA reduced-prefix reassembly to n=512 while restoring PyTorch zero/slice reassembly for n=1024; validation passed and geomean improved to 96486.170298 us.
Tried row-block CUDA reduced reassembly kernels to reduce modulo/index overhead; validation passed but benchmark regressed to 96507.614855 us versus the prior n=512-only assembly best.
Tested limiting CUDA reduced reassembly further to n=512 rank384 while sending rank258 back through PyTorch zero/slice reassembly; validation passed but geomean regressed to 96571.477846 us.

Best score in reduced reassembly brief was 96486.170298 us at commit 3b44bec0467b54f2a8d542dc470be2e7caa9762a. Full CUDA C++ assembly for both n=512 and n=1024 validated and improved to 96534.999275 us; limiting CUDA assembly to n=512 while restoring PyTorch zero/slice for n=1024 improved further. Row-block assembly kernels and rank384-only n512 gating both validated but regressed, suggesting the original grid-stride CUDA assembler is best for n512 and n1024 prefers PyTorch reassembly. Final best was profiled for the next brief.

Replace the existing n=176 CUDA C++ Householder QR path with a cooperative multi-warp panel kernel using shared-memory column tiles and warp-level reductions, starting with four warps per matrix and falling back to two only if occupancy/register pressure dominates, aiming to reduce global-memory traffic while preserving geqrf H/tau semantics and all other shape dispatch.
Four-warp n=176 panel QR attempt built but validation failed on the n=176 fixed test with H containing NaN/Inf; likely the tiled dot-product reduction mixed columns within a warp.

Corrected segmented warp tile reduction for the four-warp n=176 panel kernel, but validation still failed n=176 reconstruction because dot products were only reduced within each warp, not across all four warps.
Added cross-warp coefficient accumulation to the four-warp n=176 panel kernel, but validation still failed n=176 reconstruction because the pivot-row contribution was included once per warp.

Replaced the n=176 QR path with a four-warp cooperative panel kernel that tiles four columns, uses warp-level segmented dot reductions plus cross-warp coefficient accumulation, and preserves geqrf H/tau semantics; validation passed and geomean improved to 90576.984412 us.
Tried a two-warp n=176 panel fallback with 64 threads and two-warp reductions; it built but failed the n=176 fixed validation reconstruction, so four warps remain the only valid panel variant.
Tried widening the valid four-warp n=176 panel kernel to an 8-column tile with two lanes per column; it built but failed n=176 reconstruction validation, so the 4-column tile remains best.

Best score in n=176 panel brief was 90576.984412 us at commit d57ae92bd76130b738990deec1ccb2192092eb73. The successful custom CUDA C++ change replaced the one-block n=176 Householder QR with a four-warp cooperative panel kernel using four-column tiles, segmented warp dot reductions, and shared cross-warp coefficient accumulation while preserving geqrf H/tau semantics. Initial versions failed validation until column-segment reduction, cross-warp summing, and single pivot-row contribution were fixed; two-warp and 8-column tile variants both built but failed validation. Final best was profiled for the next brief.

Profile the four-warp n=176 QR kernel for the dominant stall source, then run a focused sweep of one bottleneck: tile width and per-warp row ownership if occupancy/barriers dominate, or coefficient/shared-memory layout if bank conflicts dominate; preserve geqrf semantics and all non-n176 dispatch.

Profile showed latency/occupancy pressure rather than bank conflicts; removed the extra shared coeffs array and one synchronization per n=176 panel tile by storing tau-scaled per-warp coefficients directly in warp_coeffs. Validation passed and geomean improved to 90097.448852 us.
Tried an 8-column/four-row-per-column n=176 tile with the direct coefficient layout; it built but failed n=176 reconstruction validation, so TILE=4 remains the valid layout.
Padded the n=176 panel warp_coeffs shared-memory rows from TILE to stride 8 after the direct tau-scaled coefficient layout; validation passed and geomean improved slightly to 90064.108336 us.
Tested widening n=176 panel warp_coeffs padding from stride 8 to stride 16; validation passed, but geomean was 90065.267767 us, a slight regression versus stride 8.

Best score in n=176 micro sweep was 90064.108336 us at commit 998f0affaacc3d5c3de9269fedbcf674d56fd7bb. The n176-specific profile still captured a PyTorch elementwise launch, but indicated latency/occupancy pressure rather than bank conflicts; focusing on coefficient/shared-memory layout, removing the extra coeffs array and barrier improved to 90097.448852 us, then padding warp_coeffs rows to stride 8 improved slightly further. An 8-column/four-row ownership variant failed validation, and stride 16 validated but regressed slightly. Final best was profiled for the next brief.

Selectively port only the n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular early-reject CUDA detector/fast path from 31ae into 03ce, preserving 03ce's n=32, n=176, n=352, n=512, n=1024, homogeneous fast paths, and fallbacks; gate before detector launch and avoid added dense n=4096 batch=2 overhead.

Selectively ported 31ae's CUDA n=4096 upper-triangular detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path into 03ce, gated to batch=1 before launching the detector so dense benchmark batch=2 avoids overhead. Validation passed and geomean improved to 90032.341985 us.

Combined only the n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular detector/fast path from 31ae into parent 03ce, preserving 03ce's n=32/176/352/512/1024 paths and gating on batch=1 before launching the detector to avoid dense batch=2 overhead. The combined candidate validated and scored 90032.341985 us at commit b8036a26259bfb85a1af60627f8ace407761cd71. Final upper-shape profile was captured for the next brief; further n4096 benefit would require an active benchmark upper case or eliminating the H clone for test-only upper.

Starting from cf9e global best, selectively port only b803's n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular early-reject detector/fast path, preserving cf9e's custom n=512 rank-384 prefix QR, n=352 cuSOLVER, n=176/n=32 kernels, n=1024 paths, homogeneous fast paths, and all fallbacks; verify dispatch is unchanged for n=512/n=1024 and batch>1.

Starting from cf9e global best, selectively ported b803's CUDA n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path, preserving existing n=32/176/352/512/1024 dispatch and gating before detector launch for batch>1. Validation passed and geomean improved to 88367.783951 us.

Starting from cf9e global best, ported only b803's n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular early-reject detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path. Existing n=32/n=176/n=352/n=512/n=1024 dispatch and fallbacks were preserved, and the new detector is gated on batch=1 before launch so n=4096 batch>1 falls through unchanged. Validation passed and benchmark scored 88367.783951 us at commit c45d824aa2100f8b1eeb2d76349c27e6c5c1c73f; final upper-shape profile was captured.

Starting from 47ba and c45d, surgically port only c45d's n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular detector with H=A,tau=0 fast path; preserve 47ba's n=512 rank-384/rank-258 sync-free CUDA prefix QR, n=352 cuSOLVER, n=176/n=32 kernels, n=1024 paths, homogeneous fast paths, and batch>1 fallbacks unchanged.

Starting from 47ba, surgically ported c45d's CUDA n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path, preserving sync-free n=512 rank384/rank258 prefix QR, n=352 cuSOLVER, n=176/n=32, n=1024 paths, and batch>1 fallbacks. Validation passed and geomean improved to 86031.540027 us.

Starting from 47ba, ported only c45d's n=4096 batch=1 upper-triangular detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path. The n=512 rank384/rank258 sync-free CUDA prefix QR, n=352 cuSOLVER, n=176/n=32 kernels, n=1024 paths, homogeneous fast paths, and batch>1 fallbacks were preserved; the detector is gated before launch on batch=1. Validation passed and benchmark scored 86031.540027 us at commit c619073f7dd82a2587396ad4ce305c6556b215ec; final upper-shape profile was captured.

Starting from 34723e, measure n512 homogeneous dispatch/classification overhead first, then replace only the Python/Torch all-rank384/all-rank258 predicates with the cheapest safe device-side or C++ host-side classifier that avoids extra synchronization; keep mixed n512 on torch.geqrf and leave QR kernels/fallbacks unchanged. Abandon unless benchmark shows clear net win over 34723e.

First n512 C++ homogeneous classifier used a fixed host flag buffer sized for benchmark batch=640; validation invariance guard exercised larger n512 batch and classify_n512_homogeneous returned cudaErrorInvalidValue. Logging before fixing per workflow.

Replaced n512 Python/Torch homogeneous all-rank384/all-rank258 predicates with a C++ classifier using one detect launch and one device-to-host copy, leaving mixed n512 to torch.geqrf. Validation passed, but benchmark regressed versus measured parent 85377.416348 to 86116.546094, so abandoning.

Brief 10 exhausted. Measured parent 34723e at 85377.416348. Tried two C++ n512 homogeneous classifiers: first device-reduction version validated after fix but benchmarked 89280.004110; leaner one-detect/one-D2H C++ classifier validated and benchmarked 86116.546094. Both regressed, especially mixed n512 falling to torch.geqrf as requested, so branch reset to parent 34723e and no optimization kept. Final parent profile captured.

From c3b4, micro-tune only the homogeneous n512 CUDA prefix-QR path: profile the current 64-thread kernel for occupancy/registers/sync stalls, then test exactly one narrower occupancy variant, preferably 32-thread blocks with corresponding warp/reduction ownership changes. Preserve homogeneous-only n512 dispatch, keep mixed n512 on torch.geqrf, and leave n352/n176/n32/n1024/n4096 paths unchanged.

Tested exactly one narrower homogeneous n512 prefix-QR occupancy variant: reduced qr512_prefix_kernel block width/reduction ownership from 64 to 32 threads, preserving n512 dispatch and all other paths. Validation passed and benchmark scored 84838.714731 us, essentially flat/slightly regressed versus parent c3b4 84835.997 us.

Brief 11 exhausted. Profiled parent c3b4; tested exactly one narrower n512 homogeneous prefix-QR occupancy/warp-ownership variant by reducing block width from 64 to 32 threads, preserving dispatch and all non-n512 paths. The variant validated but scored 84838.714731 us versus parent c3b4's logged 84835.997 us, so reset branch to parent c3b4 and kept no new optimization. Final parent profile captured.

Starting from c3b4, cherry-pick only c619's n4096 batch=1 upper-triangular CUDA detector and H=A,tau=0 fast path behind an exact n==4096 && batch==1 gate; keep c3b4 n512/n352/n176/n32/n1024 and batch>1 dispatch byte-for-byte where possible, benchmark overhead carefully, and abandon if any non-n4096 routing or timing regresses.

Combined c619's n4096 batch=1 upper-triangular CUDA detector and H=A,tau=0 clone fast path onto c3b4 behind an exact n==4096 && batch==1 gate after existing n512/n1024 dispatch. c3b4 dispatch outside that gated path is otherwise unchanged. Validation passed; benchmark confirmed improvement to 83901.920019 us after an initial noisy 85115.145519 run.

Combine brief 12 complete. Starting from c3b4, ported only c619's n4096 batch=1 upper-triangular CUDA detector plus H=A,tau=0 clone fast path, strictly gated on data.shape[0] == 1 and shape[1:] == (4096,4096) after existing c3b4 dispatch. n512/n352/n176/n32/n1024 and batch>1 dispatch remain unchanged. Validation/guards passed; benchmark best confirmed at 83901.920019 us, improving over c3b4's logged 84835.997 us. Final ncu profile captured.

Profile 1567's exact n==4096 && batch==1 upper-triangular fast path, then tune only measured H-clone/tau-zero overhead using safe CUDA C++ fill/copy or alias-preserving clone elision behind the same strict detector gate; keep all other dispatch unchanged and abandon on validation failure or any non-n4096/batch>1 timing regression.

Profiled 1567 first, then tuned only the exact-gated n4096 upper fast path by eliding the H clone and returning the input alias with zero tau. Validation and guards passed, but benchmarks regressed to 85610.526178 and 85113.344575 versus parent 83901.920019, so abandoning.

Brief 13 exhausted. Parent/profile 1567's exact-gated n4096 upper path showed only tiny elementwise/tau-zero work in ncu; tested the measured H-clone overhead by returning the input alias instead of data.clone() behind the unchanged n==4096 && batch==1 detector gate. The alias variant validated but benchmarked 85610.526178 then 85113.344575, regressing versus parent 83901.920019, so branch reset to 1567 and no optimization kept. Parent ncu profile captured before editing.

Profile parent 1567 and tune exactly one detector-local bottleneck in the strict n==4096 && batch==1 upper-triangular CUDA detector—prefer lower-triangle tile geometry or warp/block reduction/early-exit mechanics—while preserving exact detection semantics, H=A clone, tau-zero behavior, and all other dispatch paths unchanged; abandon on validation failure or geomean regression.

Tuned exactly one detector-local n4096 bottleneck: replaced lower-triangle linear-index binary search with row-wise lower-triangle scanning inside detect_n4096_upper, preserving detection semantics, H clone/tau-zero behavior, exact gate, and all other dispatch. Validation passed but geomean regressed to 86711.051729 versus parent 83901.920019, so abandoning.

Brief 14 exhausted. Profiled the exact n4096 upper spec, then tuned exactly one detector-local bottleneck by replacing the binary-search lower-triangle index mapping in detect_n4096_upper with row-wise lower-triangle scanning. H=A clone, tau-zero behavior, strict n==4096 && batch==1 gate, and all other dispatch were preserved. Validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 86711.051729 versus parent 83901.920019, so branch reset to 1567 and no optimization kept.

Starting from 1567, profile n2048 active cases and inspect inputs for cheap exact structure. Add an exact-gated custom CUDA C++ n2048 fast path only if a high-frequency case is detected, e.g. upper-triangular/zero-tail rank pattern using H=A,tau=0 or geqrf-prefix plus minimal CUDA reassembly. Preserve all existing n512/n4096/n352/n176/n32/n1024 dispatches; require validation and geomean improvement, otherwise abandon.

Brief 15 exhausted without code changes. Profiled the active n2048 benchmark spec and inspected n2048 active/test inputs for exact upper-triangular or rank/zero-tail structure. The active benchmark batch=8,n=2048,cond=1 dense case has no exact zero tail and is not upper triangular; test-only rankdef has zero tail but is not active, and mixed/dense cases lack a safe exact structure. Prior in-run n2048 cuSOLVER pack/unpack attempts validated but regressed when combined. Per brief, no exact-gated custom CUDA C++ n2048 fast path was added because no high-frequency exact structure was detected and adding detector overhead would risk geomean regression. Existing n512/n4096/n352/n176/n32/n1024 dispatch remains unchanged.

Starting from 1567, replace only the n4096 batch=1 true-upper fast path with one exact-gated CUDA C++ kernel that detects upper-triangular structure and, only on success, copies A to H and zeros tau in-kernel; preserve existing fallback and all other sizes/paths byte-for-byte; explicitly handle alias/contiguity/strides like current code; abandon on validation failure or geomean regression.

Replaced only the n4096 batch=1 true-upper fast path with an exact-gated fused CUDA C++ detector/copy/tau-zero kernel, preserving fallback and non-n4096 dispatch. Validation passed, but benchmarks regressed to 85140.345033 and 85191.506706 versus parent 83901.920019, so abandoning.

Brief 16 exhausted. Implemented a fused exact-gated n4096 batch=1 upper fast path that detects upper-triangular structure and, on success only, copies A to H and zeros tau in one CUDA C++ kernel; fallback and all non-n4096 dispatch paths were preserved. Validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed twice (85140.345033 and 85191.506706) versus parent 83901.920019, so branch reset to 1567 and no optimization kept.

For n4096 batch=1 only, add a tiny exact-safe lower-triangle sample probe before the existing upper detector to reject obvious dense/non-upper inputs; never classify as upper from samples, fall through on uncertainty, and keep only if dense n4096 improves with no true-upper or geomean regression.

Added a tiny exact-safe n4096 batch=1 lower-triangle sample probe before the existing upper detector. The probe only rejects obvious non-upper inputs and never classifies samples as upper; uncertainty falls through to the full detector. Validation passed, but geomean regressed to 85162.532666 versus parent 83901.920019, so abandoning.

Brief 17 exhausted. Added a reject-only exact-safe lower-triangle sample probe for n4096 batch=1 before the existing full upper detector. The probe only rejected obvious non-upper samples and never accepted/classified upper from samples; uncertain cases fell through to the full detector and true-upper behavior was preserved. Validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 85162.532666 versus parent 83901.920019, so branch reset to 1567 and no optimization kept.

Reset to baseline and inspect active qr_v2 input shapes in-code with zero-output, compile-time/constant-shape gated predicates only; implement one exact CUDA C++ fast path for a cheap structure not covered by n512 reduced-rank or n4096 upper, prioritizing diagonal/identity/zero-column or already-triangular cases. No persistent logging or benchmark-time profiling; keep only if validated and faster than baseline, with a small isolated diff suitable to combine onto 1567.

Attempted one exact n512 rankdef zero-tail CUDA C++ path from baseline, but the first build failed because load_inline generated a duplicate PYBIND11 module for the manually declared binding; fixing binding and retrying.

Fixed the load_inline binding and built the exact n512 rankdef zero-tail path, but full validation failed on the n512 rankdef test because the reassembled square compact factors produced NaN/Inf in householder_product; investigating the compact-factor edge before deciding whether to abandon.
